answer: A meteg appears to be printed: there is a short vertical stroke under the word. Its host letter cannot be confirmed. The stroke sits under the middle of the word, near the mem and next to the sheva (:) and the tsere (two dots), not clearly under the shin. The host could be the mem (with sheva), or it could be the shin/holam stroke printed out of place. Host letter and vowel: unresolved.
visible_evidence: The whole word שומרנו is visible, including its lower points. Below the word there are three marks, from left to right in the image: a short isolated vertical stroke at about x≈165, two dots side by side (a tsere) at about x≈180–200, and a colon-shaped sheva at about x≈205. The stroke does not look like part of a letter's stem. It is separate from the dots and well above the next line's ink, so it is most likely a meteg. However, it lines up with the mem/resh area of the word, not clearly with any one letter, and it sits right next to the sheva. That position is unusual for a meteg, so I can't name the host letter with confidence.
